label: first token is y (t=0, input y)
explanation: Fires on exactly one step per sequence: step 0 when the first original token is the letter y. Precision and recall on the dev split are both 1.0. The activation is constant at 0.106 (binary, so nothing modulates its size). It does not fire on y at any later position, on any other token at t=0, or anywhere in the delimiter or copy phases. Sequence length has no effect beyond the base rate.

issues: None found. On the dev profile, all 16824 active steps are at t=0 with in_tok=y. The rate is 0 at every other t, in the delimiter phase and in the copy phase, and it is 0 for every other in_tok, including y at later positions.
Test split: precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, correlation ~1.0. The misses command returned 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.
The magnitude really is constant: mean, median and max are all 0.106.

The firing rate by L does vary (2.1x down to 0.7x), but that is explained by longer sequences having more steps. Each sequence fires at most once, so the 'no length effect beyond base rate' claim holds.
